Subject: RFP commercial question — smoothing / escape clauses

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. The procurement team reviewed your draft commercial term sheet and has two follow-ups specific to our risk profile:

1) We expect high volatility during pilot -> production ramp. We need a mechanism to avoid punitive overage charges in months where traffic spikes 3-4x (for a short window).
2) We also need an explicit "tier escape" path: if we materially change usage patterns (new product feature that increases per-session tokens), we want a defined rebase process rather than automatic overage billing.

Can Redwood outline options for a) temporary usage credits or burst cushions and b) a formalized rebase/escape process tied to a short notice period? Please include how credits are funded, when they expire, and any pricing impact.

If useful, I've attached a sample monthly usage profile and our RFP pricing worksheet.

Best,
Elena
Head of Procurement
Medisys

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the usage profile, that helps. High level answer below; attaching an updated term sheet (v3) that incorporates a pragmatic safeguard construct.

Short answer summary:
- Burst cushion: we offer a monthly "burst credit" pool sized as a percentage of committed monthly tokens (default 50% of MCT) that can be consumed in any month and expires at month-end. Credits are applied before overage invoicing.
- Escalation/rebase ("tier escape"): We provide a one-time rebase window tied to contract quarters: if sustained 2x+ usage for 6 consecutive weeks, either party can trigger a rebase review. Pricing during the review is held at a capped blended rate for 30 days while we agree on new bands; overages during the 30-day window convert to credits if new bands are executed.
- Funding & economics: Burst credits are effectively a waived upfront charge (no pre-pay required) but we expect them to be sized conservatively for enterprise customers; larger credit pools can be included in exchange for a higher commit or lower unit price.

I've put the detailed mechanics in the term sheet: how credits apply, examples with token math, and a sample rebase timeline.

Next steps: Ben and I can run a short pricing sensitivity with your usage sheet and propose two options: 1) Aggressive cushion + mid-tier commit with moderate discount, 2) Lower cushion + larger commit with deeper discount. Which would you like us to model?

Thanks — attaching: 20270630-Redwood-commercial-term-sheet-v3.pdf

Regards,
Irene Choi

Redwood Inference

Irene — this looks promising. A couple clarifying questions from procurement: 

- For the burst credit pool that expires month-end, can unused credits carry for one additional month in the event of a major outage that prevented usage? (We want to avoid losing cushion because of deployment delays.)
- For the rebase window: how do you define "sustained 2x+"? Our engineers are worried about short-term load tests accidentally triggering a rebase. Could you tie the trigger to production traffic excluding load-test IP ranges?

Also, our legal team asked whether the capped blended rate during review is guaranteed not to exceed the existing list rate — we prefer a cap not to increase our cost during negotiations.

If you can confirm those, we'll share an internal preference (option 1 vs 2) by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Elena

Subject: Fwd: RFP commercial question — suggested language for legal and ops

Irene / Rishi — forwarding Medisys questions. Draft suggested language below for legal to review; this is intentionally conservative:

1) Burst cushion carryover (exception): In the event of a documented platform outage attributable to Redwood or a mutually-agreed deployment delay, up to 100% of unused burst credits from the impacted month may be carried into the immediately following month. Documentation to be provided within 14 days.

2) Rebase trigger definition: "Sustained 2x+" is defined as observed customer traffic (as measured by server-side token ingress) exceeding 200% of Customer's average monthly baseline for six (6) consecutive calendar weeks, excluding traffic identified in a mutually-agreed load-test IP list. Redwood and Customer will mutually agree on the baseline window at contract execution.

3) Pricing cap during review: During the 30-day rebase review window, Redwood will apply a capped blended rate not to exceed Customer's effective list rate at time of trigger. Any retroactive differences resolved by rebase execution will be credited to the customer if the new bands result in lower pricing.

I've kept the credit funding model as non-prepaid but we can offer a partially-prepaid cushion (e.g., 25% of annual commit) in exchange for deeper unit discounts — that will be our commercial lever.

Thoughts? If we agree, I'll ask legal to draft contract language for inclusion in the SOW/Amendment.

-Ben
